What is your overall wedding style or th: Share your style with your vendors
Pick one phrase and give it to every vendor. It keeps flowers, stationery and decor telling the same story.
What are your top three priorities for t: Move budget toward your top three priorities
Spend on the three things you care about and go simple on everything else.
Will you offer plus-ones, and what is th: Write the plus-one rule on the website
One clear rule applied to everyone avoids hurt feelings.
Are children invited?: Address invitations to show who is invited
Name every invited person on the envelope. “Adults only” goes on the website, not the invitation.
Who is officiating?: Book the officiant and set planning calls

Who is walking the bride down the aisle?: Confirm who walks down the aisle with whom
Who holds the rings until the ceremony?: Give the rings to their keeper before the ceremony
Use the real rings, not a pillow, with an adult. Decoys go on the ring bearer.
Who will sign the marriage license as wi: Tell the witnesses when and where to sign
Check how many witnesses your county needs, and their minimum age.
Are there family dynamics the planner an: Brief the planner, photographer and DJ on family dynamics
Vendors handle this discreetly every weekend, but only if they are told.
Are there any people who should not be s: Mark who must be apart on the seating chart
Are any guests elderly, pregnant, or hav: Reserve aisle seats and arrange help for guests who need it
Have you walked the full guest route (pa: Walk the guest route with the venue
Walk it yourself from the parking lot: doors, steps, gravel, restrooms, distance.
Which family photo groupings are must-ha: Send the family photo list to the photographer
Write real names, not “bride’s family”. Order it so grandparents go first and can sit down.
Is there a must-have shot list beyond th: Send the must-have shot list to the photographer
What is the meal service style?: Confirm the meal style and choices with the caterer
Plated is slowest but calmest. Buffets need one line per 50 guests.
Any special dietary needs for the head t: Send allergies and dietary needs to the caterer
Do you have a rain backup plan for the c: Write the rain plan into the schedule
If you would be heartbroken by plan B, make plan B nicer now.
Who makes the weather call, and by what: Set the weather-call time and who decides
Make the call early enough for rentals and florist to change setup, usually by mid-morning.
Who is the day-of point of contact?: Give every vendor the day-of contact
It should not be either of you, or a parent.
Who confirms vendor arrival times the we: Confirm vendor arrival times the week before
Who is contributing to the budget, and a: Confirm contributions and any conditions in writing
Ask how much, when it arrives, and whether it comes with a say in decisions.
Who mails the signed marriage license ba: Confirm who files the marriage license
Most states give only a few days. Ask the officiant to send a photo once it is mailed.
How many guests do you expect?: Count on about 80 to 85 percent of invited guests saying yes.
Are passports valid at least six months: Renewals can take months. Book travel in the name on the passport.
Do you have inspiration photos or Pinter: Share your inspiration board with vendors
Will there be a welcome event or welcome: Plan the welcome event or welcome bags
Is there a wedding hashtag or photo-shar: Put the hashtag or photo link on signs
Will there be a video or livestream for: Arrange a livestream and test the signal
Test the signal at the ceremony spot. Give one person the job of starting it.
Will there be a unity ceremony?: Buy what is needed for the unity ceremony
Will the ceremony be unplugged (no guest: Ask the officiant to announce an unplugged ceremony
Are pets part of the ceremony?: A handler takes the pet home straight after photos.
Will the wedding party be introduced at: Send introductions and name pronunciations to the DJ
Are there roles for close friends not in: Ask friends to take on special roles
Will there be a receiving line?: Decide between a receiving line and table visits
Table visits take about two minutes a table. Do them during dinner.
Is there anyone the photographer should: Tell the photographer who to avoid
Do you want a second shooter, drone foot: Decide on photo and video add-ons
Will there be a bouquet or garter toss?: Tell the DJ which traditions you are skipping
Is there a guest book or alternative?: Buy the guest book and supplies
Is there a favor for guests?: Edible favors get taken home. Most others are left on the table.
Will there be a send-off?: Confirm the venue allows your send-off
Signature cocktails?: Choose signature cocktails with the bartender
When is last call?: Set last call with the bartender
What is the cake flavor?: Choose cake flavors at a tasting
Will there be a cake cutting, a dessert: Confirm cake and dessert plans with the baker
Will you save the top tier of the cake?: Ask the baker to box the top tier
What is the plan for leftover food and f: Arrange containers and a home for leftovers
Who has the emergency kit?: Safety pins, fashion tape, stain pen, sewing kit, pain relief, blister pads, phone chargers.
Who is preserving the dress and bouquet?: The bouquet needs to reach the preserver within a day or two.
Will you change your name?: List where your name needs changing
Social Security first, then license, passport, bank.
How did you meet? (for the officiant and: Send your story to the officiant
Are there inside jokes or stories to inc: Share stories with whoever is giving toasts
Will there be surprise moments (gifts to: Plan any surprise moments with the planner
Tell the planner and photographer, even if nobody else knows.
Will you exchange letters or gifts with: Write letters or buy gifts for each other
What is the one moment you most want to: Tell the photographer the moment you most want captured
Is there anything you definitely do NOT: Tell your vendors what you do not want
What season and time of day feels right: Choose the season and time of day
How many guests are coming from out of t: Size the hotel block for out-of-town guests
What is the dress code for guests?: Put the dress code on the website
Mention the ground underfoot (grass, sand, cobblestones) so guests choose shoes that work.
How will guests RSVP (card, website, or: Number the back of each RSVP card to match your list. Someone always forgets to write their name.
Are you writing your own vows?: Agree a rough length with each other so one is not three lines and the other three pages.
Who are the ushers, and who gets reserve: Brief the ushers on reserved seating
Will there be a first look?: Add the first look to the schedule
A first look lets you finish most photos before the ceremony and join your own cocktail hour.
Who pays for wedding party attire and ha: Tell the wedding party what they are paying for
Where will the wedding party get ready?: Pick rooms with good window light and enough mirrors and outlets.
Who is giving toasts?: Ask each person giving a toast
Should a family member help gather peopl: Ask a family member to gather people for photos
Will there be a grand entrance, and who: Send entrance details to the DJ
Which special dances are planned?: Choose songs for the special dances
Ask the DJ to fade long songs at about two minutes.
Any songs that should NOT be played?: Send the do-not-play list to the DJ
Are there names the DJ or officiant shou: Send name pronunciations to the DJ and officiant
What are the venue rules (candles, confe: Get the venue rules in writing
Is there a noise curfew or a hard end ti: Confirm the end time and curfew with the venue
Do vendors need a meal and a place to ea: Add vendor meals to the final count
Count every vendor who is there through dinner, and feed them when guests eat.
Where can vendors park and load in?: Send vendors parking and load-in details
Who takes gifts and cards home?: Assign someone to take gifts and cards home
Cards hold cash. Use a box that closes and move it out of sight after dinner.
Who is the backup if the planner is unav: Name a backup for the planner
Where are you willing to splurge, and wh: Adjust the budget for splurges and savings
How much is set aside for emergencies?: Five to ten percent of the budget is the usual cushion.
Honeymoon plans?: Consider leaving a day or two after the wedding, not the next morning.
Is there a guest shuttle, or will guests: Shuttles should leave the hotel 45 minutes before the ceremony, and run at least twice at the end.
When will thank-you cards go out, and wh: Write a few a day. Record each gift as cards are opened.
When and where will you get the marriage: Licenses expire (often in 30 to 90 days) and some counties have a waiting period. Too early or too late both cause problems.
Who is the “license captain” who brings: Give the license to the license captain at the rehearsal
On the day nobody remembers the license. One named person makes sure it is signed before the officiant leaves.
Is your officiant legally able to marry: Confirm the officiant’s credentials with the county clerk
A friend who gets ordained online still has to meet the county rules, and some counties ask for registration ahead of time.
Do you want a prenuptial agreement, and: Meet with an attorney about a prenup
A prenup signed in the last few weeks can be challenged. Attorneys usually want it finished at least a month before.
How many certified copies of the marriag: Order certified copies of the marriage certificate
Each name change (Social Security, license, passport, bank) may want its own certified copy. Ordering them together saves weeks.
After the wedding, what needs updating (: Update insurance and beneficiaries after the wedding
Marriage is a qualifying event. Most health plans only give you 30 to 60 days to add a spouse.
Will you buy wedding insurance (cancella: A few hundred dollars protects every deposit if a vendor closes, someone gets sick or weather shuts the venue. Many venues also require liability cover.
Does the venue require proof of insuranc: Collect insurance certificates from vendors for the venue
Vendors can be turned away at the door if the venue has no certificate of insurance on file.
What does each contract say about cancel: Note the cancellation deadline for each vendor
Know which deposits are refundable and until when. It is the first thing you will need if plans change.
What are each vendor’s overtime rates, a: Write overtime rates on the vendor list
Overtime is the most common surprise bill. Agree the rate now and name one person who can say yes.
Are there service charges, taxes, cake-c: Ask each vendor for an all-in total in writing
A 22% service charge plus tax can add a quarter to the catering bill. Ask for the all-in number.
If a vendor cannot make it (illness, eme: Ask solo vendors who their backup is
Solo photographers, DJs and officiants should name who covers for them. It should be in the contract.
When is the final headcount due, and can: Put the final headcount deadline on the calendar
After the guarantee date you pay for every plate, even if guests cancel.
What time is sunset, and when is the bes: Check the sunset time and add golden-hour photos to the schedule
Golden hour is about an hour before sunset. The whole evening timeline should be built around it.
What time must hair and makeup be comple: Get a hair and makeup schedule from the stylist
Work backwards from the first photo. Add 30 minutes of cushion, and schedule the bride second to last, not last.
Is there buffer time between the big mom: Everything runs 10 to 15 minutes long. A timeline with no cushion is late by dinner.
How do guests get from the ceremony to c: Assign someone to direct guests between spaces
The moments between events are where guests get lost. Signs help, a person helps more.
Will the two of you take 10 quiet minute: Add private time for the couple to the schedule
It is often the only time you are alone all day. Ask the caterer to bring you a plate and a drink.
When will you actually eat, and who make: Ask the caterer to serve the couple first and box a late meal
Couples often leave their own wedding hungry. Have the caterer serve you first and box a meal for later.
Does every vendor’s booked time cover th: Compare each vendor’s hours to the schedule
Photographers booked for eight hours often leave before the cake or the exit. Check start and end times against the schedule.
Who gets a copy of the final timeline, a: Send the final timeline to vendors and family
Vendors, the wedding party and close family each need it a week ahead. Family only needs their own times.
What happens at the venue between guests: Make a breakdown plan with names next to each job
Someone has to pack decor, gifts, leftover alcohol and personal items inside the venue’s time limit.
When are your fittings, and who is comin: Book fittings and bring the bustle helper to the last one
The person doing the bustle should see it done once. Film it on a phone at the final fitting.
Have you booked hair and makeup trials?: Book the hair and makeup trial
Do the trial on the day of a shower or the engagement photos so it does double duty.
Who steams and transports the dress, sui: Arrange steaming for the morning of
Dresses wrinkle in the car. Decide who owns the steamer and when it happens.
Do you have a second pair of shoes and a: Buy backup shoes and break in the wedding pair
New shoes for ten hours is the most common regret. Break them in at home and bring flats.
When do the rings need to be sized, engr: Order and size the wedding bands
Engraving and sizing can take four to six weeks. Have them in hand two weeks before.
What are the groom and groomsmen wearing: Send suit measurements and set the pickup date
Out-of-town groomsmen need to send measurements early. Everyone tries the suit on at pickup, not on the day.
Do you need two boutonnieres or a spare: Ask the florist for a spare boutonniere
Boutonnieres get crushed by hugs before the ceremony. A spare costs a few dollars.
What will guests need for the weather (s: Order weather comfort items for guests
A basket of fans or blankets costs little and is what guests remember about being looked after.
Are there enough restrooms, and are they: Check restroom count and add a restroom basket
Plan about one restroom per 50 guests. A small basket with basics is a kind touch.
How do guests who have been drinking get: Arrange a safe-ride plan for guests
Decide the plan before the bar opens: shuttles, ride-share codes or a car service number at the door.
Is there a quiet place for nursing mothe: Ask the venue for a quiet room
A side room with chairs keeps families at the party longer.
Will there be childcare, a kids’ table o: Plan kids’ activities or a sitter
Even two children do better with a small activity bag at their seats.
What will you do if someone brings an un: Ask the caterer to hold two extra meals
Have the caterer hold two extra meals and keep two blank place cards. Then it is a non-event.
How will guests find their seats (chart,: Order the seating chart or escort cards
Alphabetical by last name is fastest. A chart by table number makes a line.
What should out-of-town guests know (air: Add travel details to the wedding website
Put it on the website once and you will answer it far fewer times by text.
Does any guest need an interpreter, larg: Arrange accessibility help for guests who need it
Ask close family. People rarely volunteer this themselves.
When and where is the rehearsal, and who: Send rehearsal details to everyone in the ceremony
Everyone who walks, reads or holds something attends. Tell them an arrival time 15 minutes early.
Who runs the rehearsal?: Usually the coordinator, not the officiant. One voice keeps it to 30 minutes.
Who hosts the rehearsal dinner, who is i: Book the rehearsal dinner and send invitations
Traditionally the groom’s family hosts. Long toasts belong here, not at the reception.
What will you hand over at the rehearsal: Make a hand-off list for the rehearsal
The rehearsal is the last calm moment to pass things to the people responsible.
Will there be a shower, bachelor or bach: Share guest lists and dates with the party hosts
Give the hosts a guest list and two or three dates. Everyone invited to a shower should be invited to the wedding.
What will you each do the morning of the: Order breakfast and lunch for both getting-ready rooms
Plan a real breakfast and something calm. Order food for both getting-ready rooms in advance.
If the ceremony moves indoors, what exac: Write out the rain plan and send it to vendors
A rain plan is only real if the florist, musicians, rentals and photographer all know their part of it.
Do outdoor vendors have the power they n: Confirm power needs with the venue and each vendor
Bands, DJs, lighting and caterers each need their own circuit. One tripped breaker stops the music.
Who has a spare copy of the vows, readin: Print spare copies of vows, readings and timeline
Phones die and notes get left in hotel rooms. Printed spares with the coordinator fix it in seconds.
Who is the emergency contact for each of: Share emergency contacts and medical notes with the planner
Allergies, medication and a named contact take one minute to share and matter a great deal if needed.
What is the plan if a key person is late: Name a stand-in for each key role
Decide the latest you will wait and who steps in. You will probably never use it.
Where are the nearest pharmacy, urgent c: Add the nearest pharmacy and urgent care to Places
Someone will need safety pins, pain relief or a phone charger. Knowing where saves a search.
Who holds your phones, keys, wallet and: Assign someone to hold personal items
Wedding clothes have no pockets. One person with one bag ends the question.
How do you want the day to feel, in thre: Share your three words with your vendors
Three words settle most small decisions later. If an idea does not fit them, drop it.
How involved do you want each set of par: Talk with both families about who decides what
Deciding this together and early prevents most family friction, especially when parents are contributing.
What is your A-list and B-list, and when: Split the guest list into first and second rounds
Send the first round ten weeks out with an early RSVP date so second-round guests still get a proper invitation.
When do save-the-dates and invitations g: Set mailing dates for save-the-dates and invitations
Save-the-dates six to eight months out, invitations eight to ten weeks out, RSVP three to four weeks before.
How will you chase people who have not r: Follow up with guests who have not replied
About one in five guests needs a reminder. Split the list by family and start the day after the deadline.
Where are you registered, and how will g: Set up the registry and link it on the website
Registry details go on the website and by word of mouth, never on the invitation itself.
Have you checked every invitation addres: Returned invitations cost two weeks. Ask each family for one person to check their side.
How long should the ceremony be, and wha: Agree the ceremony length and start time with the officiant
Print a time 15 minutes before you plan to walk. Guests arrive late and it saves a rushed start.
What music plays before, during and afte: Choose ceremony music and name who cues it
You need four cues: guests seated, processional, bride’s entrance, recessional. Someone must be able to see the aisle.
Will the officiant and readers use a mic: Outdoors, guests past the third row hear nothing without one. Test it before guests arrive.
Where does everyone stand, and will the: Tell the officiant to step aside for the first kiss
Ask the officiant to step out of the frame before the kiss. It is the photo you will frame.
Who seats the grandparents and parents,: Assign someone to cue the processional
Without a person at the back sending people down the aisle, the spacing falls apart.
Who hands out programs, and what happens: Assign bouquet, rings and vow-card duties
Decide who takes the bouquet and who has the vow cards so nobody is searching pockets.
What do you expect from the wedding part: Send the wedding party their dates, costs and duties
Tell people the costs and dates before they say yes. It keeps friendships intact.
Will you give gifts to the wedding party: Order wedding party and parent gifts
The rehearsal dinner is the natural moment. Personalized items need four to six weeks.
Who looks after the flower girl and ring: Assign an adult to the flower girl and ring bearer
Small children need a familiar adult in the front row and a plan if they refuse to walk.
Where will divorced or remarried parents: Confirm ceremony seating with each parent
Settle this privately with each parent well ahead. Surprises on the day hurt.
Who sits at the tables nearest the two o: Place family tables on the seating chart
Parents, grandparents and the wedding party closest. Put the loudest table near the dance floor and older guests away from speakers.
How much time is set aside for family ph: Share the family photo list and times with the photographer
Allow about three minutes per grouping. Ten groupings is 30 minutes, right after the ceremony while everyone is still there.
Have you told family exactly when and wh: Text family their photo time and place
The delay is always one missing uncle. Text each person their time and place the week of.
What details should the photographer cap: Pack a details box for the photographer
Put them all in one box in the getting-ready room so the photographer can start without you.
When will you get your photos and video,: Confirm photo and video delivery dates
Six to twelve weeks is normal for photos, longer for film. Ask about a sneak peek within a week.
What is the order of events at the recep: Build the reception order with the DJ
Do toasts and the first dance before or during dinner so older guests see them and the photographer is still there.
What does the DJ or band need from the v: Send the venue the entertainment setup requirements
Bands often need two to three hours to set up and sound check before guests arrive.
How will you keep the dance floor full?: Send the DJ your must-play list
Open dancing straight after a high-energy moment, keep the bar near the floor, and never close the bar during dancing.
Who gives a welcome or blessing, and do: Tell each speaker their time limit and order
Three minutes each is plenty. Ask to see toasts in advance if you are worried.
How does the night end, and what is the: Choose the last song and tell the DJ
A planned last song and exit gives the photographer the closing shot and gets guests moving to the shuttles.
When is the tasting, and who is coming?: Bring the people paying or the two of you only. Too many opinions make it harder.
How will the caterer know each guest’s m: Send the caterer meal counts by table
Meal marks on place cards plus a table-by-table list is what the kitchen needs.
How much alcohol is needed, who buys it,: Confirm the bar order and the plan for leftovers
If you supply the bar, ask whether unopened bottles can be returned, and who is the licensed bartender.
What will you offer guests who do not dr: A proper alcohol-free cocktail, not just soda, is noticed and appreciated.
When will the bar be open and closed dur: Set bar hours with the bartender
Closing the bar during dinner and toasts saves money and keeps people seated.
What time can you and your vendors get i: Confirm venue access time in writing
A late handover from an earlier event squeezes every vendor’s setup. Get the access time in writing.
Who is the venue’s person in charge on t: Get the venue coordinator’s duties in writing
A venue coordinator looks after the building, not your wedding. Know exactly where their job stops.
Where is parking, is there enough, and d: Confirm parking and drop-off with the venue
Check there is a marked accessible space and a drop-off spot near the door.
What does the venue provide, and what mu: List what the venue provides and what to rent
Ask for the full list. Missing items discovered late are the most expensive rentals.
Are permits needed (park, beach, tent, a: Public spaces and tents often need a permit weeks ahead.
Does every vendor have the day-of contac: Send vendors the final details and ask for a confirmation
Send one message a week before with all three, and ask each vendor to reply to confirm.
Who sets up the personal items (guest bo: Pack and label decor boxes for setup
Pack each table’s items in its own labeled box with a photo of how it should look.
Who makes sure rented and borrowed items: Assign someone to count and return rentals
Missing rental pieces are billed at replacement cost.
What time does each vendor need to be pa: List final payments and prepare envelopes
Pay balances before the day where you can. For anything due that day, use labeled envelopes.
What is your real total budget, and does: Add tips, tax and small costs to the budget
The items couples forget (tips, tax, alterations, postage, marriage license) add 10 to 15 percent.
How will you track who has paid what, an: Open one account or card for wedding spending
One card or one account for wedding spending makes the totals honest.
How much will you tip each vendor, and w: Decide amounts now and seal the envelopes the week before. Business owners are optional, their staff are not.
Where will you stay the night of the wed: Book the wedding-night room and send bags ahead
Send an overnight bag ahead and check you can get in late. Pack the honeymoon bags before the wedding week.
Do you need visas, vaccinations or trave: Check visas and book travel insurance
Book travel in the name on your passport. Change your name after you are home.
Who looks after your home, pets, mail an: Arrange a house and pet sitter
Gifts and cards should not sit in a car or an empty house.
Who collects personal items at the end o: Give the end-of-night collection list to one person
Give one person a written list. Things left overnight are often gone by morning.
Will you leave reviews and send thank-yo: Write vendor reviews and thank-you notes
A review is the most valuable thank-you a small vendor can get.
How will you share photos with guests, a: Set up a shared photo album and print the QR code
A shared album link or QR code on the tables gathers photos you would never otherwise see.
What family or cultural traditions matte: Ask both families about traditions to include
Ask before you plan the ceremony. It is much harder to add something meaningful at the last minute.
Is there a song, reading, recipe or obje: Choose one personal touch for each family
Small private nods (a grandmother’s recipe, a father’s song) are what families talk about afterwards.
